industry.amr: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR): bacteria that survive the antibiotics designed to kill them. Carbapenems are the last-line hospital antibiotics; carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative infections (Klebsiella, Pseudomonas, Acinetobacter, E. coli) have few options. Few companies still do antibiotic research: the chairman says eight companies started such programmes and Wockhardt is the only one to finish; big pharma largely left the field.
industry.usMarket: US: ~1.2mn Gram-negative hospital infections a year (cUTI ~600k, cIAI ~290k, HAP/VAP ~157k, BSI ~60k, other ~165k; company presentation citing an independent agency). New branded antibiotics together sell ~US$1bn a year (chairman); daily cost US$1,200-1,500. Recent launches have been slow: Shionogi's Fetroja (cefiderocol, approved 2019) was cited by an analyst at ~US$250mn; several small antibiotic developers went bankrupt after approval (e.g., Achaogen) because hospital uptake is slow and stewardship rules ration new drugs.
industry.indiaMarket: India: 600-700k Gram-negative infections a year, 35-45% carbapenem-resistant (ICMR surveillance, company); ~300 infectious-disease specialists; emerging markets carry 70-80% of the global AMR burden (company).
industry.pullIncentives: UK NHS subscription model pays a fixed fee for approved antibiotics regardless of volume (chairman: up to GBP 20mn a year; NHS 2024 round contracts run Apr-2026 to Mar-2030); the US PASTEUR Act (subscription) was not law by 30-Sep-2026; QIDP status adds 5 years of US exclusivity.
industry.biosimilarInsulin: Insulin biosimilars in India and emerging markets: a US$5.6bn opportunity with 6-7 players (company); demand growing with diabetes; tenders make quarterly sales lumpy.
industry.ukGenerics: UK generics: Wockhardt is a top-5 generic company with 18% of its covered market (hospital injectables, pharmacy, OTC, export); Pinewood is the largest generic supplier to Irish hospitals.

Or execution still under scrutiny': transformed into an innovation-led company; Zaynich approval; analyst (Business Today, Jul-2026): US needs 3-4 quarters of investment before breakeven; revenue growth slower than earlier guidance; UK GBP 20mn/yr subscription would be low-risk income

street.methodNote: No broker note standing on 30-Sep-2026 discloses a valuation method, so there is no street majority to follow (no EV/EBITDA, SOTP or Zaynich NPV is published). We use P/E on Sep-28E EPS, the yardstick the market quotes (Screener P/E) and the house method for the pharma library; the turnaround rule sets the window. A Zaynich risked NPV is shown as a sensitivity, not in the base (the own-history multiple already carries the market's pipeline premium; adding an NPV would count it twice).

moat: Six QIDP molecules, Zaynich approved in the US and India; 25 years of discovery know-how few rivals still have
Zaynich composition patent to 2038; QIDP 10-year US exclusivity; Miqnaf India patent to 2033 (expires late 2030s)
No US branded sales record; outsourced operating partner; rivals (Shionogi, AbbVie, Merck) own hospital relationships
Top-5 UK generic company, 18% covered-market share, Irish hospital leader; but generics are price-competitive
Integrated insulin API to pen; 6-7 competitors; tenders lumpy; growth 27-35%
Three Indian sites on USFDA import alert since 2013-16; US Zaynich made by a European CMO
₹3,373 cr revenue, a fraction of large Indian peers; R&D mostly capitalised
critiques: The valuation already prices a blockbuster: ~75x our Sep-28E EPS and ~40x trailing EV/EBITDA for a company whose new drug sells nothing until 2027
US antibiotic launches are notoriously slow (stewardship, hospital formularies); several approved antibiotics failed commercially
Industry record; management's own US$30-50mn first-three-years benchmark
Earnings quality: ~₹215 cr of R&D a year is capitalised, so reported EBITDA flatters; amortisation of ₹1,055 cr+ of Zaynich cost will start
Equity dilution risk: a ₹3,000 cr enabling resolution after three fund-raises in five years
Governance: promoter loans (~₹950 cr), 18.8% of promoter shares pledged, related-party IP transfers with an 85.85%-owned Swiss subsidiary whose minority holders are not named
Base business is mid-teens growth at best: UK flat in sterling, India others shrinking, emerging-market insulin lumpy
Zaynich is a single asset: a label limited to cUTI, a HAP/VAP trial still to run, and rivals (Fetroja, Emblaveo) already in hospitals
